newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY FORINT ATTACKS RESISTANCE ON NBH RATE HIKE.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY FORINT ATTACKS RESISTANCE ON NBH RATE HIKE.

text.p: Hungary's forint ended unchanged against the dollar on Tuesday, firming against the central bank's (NBH) resistance level on support from high overnight rates and the NBH's Monday rate hike, dealers said.

"After hearing yesterday's news, several market players came in and sold (foreign currency)," said WestLB Hungaria's Balazs Benczedi. "They expect from the NBH rate hike to push Tresury bill yields higher."
The forint closed at 176.60/65, at the same level where it stood at midday.
However, the Hungarian currency closed the five pip gap from the NBH resistance level, and market bids even dipped below the NBH bid, dealers said.

Dealers said the forint collected strength from high overnight interest rates and the NBH's Monday decision to raise the six-month deposit rate by 0.25 percent to 21.00 percent and to launch a one-year deposit facility at 20.50 percent.
Benczedi added that the introduction of the new NBH deposit facility increased one-year yields substantially from 20.07 percent set at a 12-month T-bill auction last week.
Hungary's overnight interest rates stood at 22.75 percent on Tuesday, high above the usual levels at around 21 percent.
Dealers said the NBH rate hike, which made savings in forints more attractive, was likely to increase interest both in foreign exchange trade on the two Budapest bourses and on the spot market.
Dealers said the forint was likely to hover in a 15-pip range below the NBH bid in a near future, though some dealers believe the forint will remain close to the central bank bid.
"We will remain at the top, at least until the interest rate level does not drop," said Szabolcs Brezina of Kereskedelmi Bank.
Foreign exchange and bond market dealers' opinions were mixed whether the NBH will keep its interest rates at the current levels for several weeks, or reduce them in the next three weeks.
The forint floats in the NBH's 4.5 percent wide intervention range, against a currency basket made up 30 percent of the dollar and 70 percent of the mark.
